0.en: Jack didn't take his eyes off the roof.
0.id: Jack tidak mengalihkan pandangan dari atap.

6.en: Mark set a hand on Aiden's shoulder, gently.
6.id: Mark menaruh tangan di bahu Aiden, lembut.

7.en: Walk like you're carrying a full cup of coffee across a room full of sleeping kids. I'll be right behind you.
7.id: Jalan seperti kamu membawa secangkir kopi penuh melintasi ruangan yang penuh anak-anak tidur. Aku tepat di belakangmu.

8.en: Aiden swallowed and started down the center aisle.
8.id: Aiden menelan ludah dan mulai menyusuri lorong tengah.

9.en: Overhead, the vent motors kept humming. One by one, the long glass panels along the roof had lifted to the height of a man and stopped there, letting the morning in. Cooler air spilled down through the openings. So did sound: the whisper of the grass, the drone of wings, the dry tick of something walking on glass.
9.id: Di atas, motor-motor ventilasi terus berdengung. Satu per satu, panel-panel kaca panjang di sepanjang atap sudah terangkat setinggi orang dewasa lalu berhenti di sana, membiarkan pagi masuk. Udara yang lebih sejuk mengalir turun lewat celah-celah itu. Begitu pula suara: bisik rumput, dengung sayap, ketukan kering sesuatu yang berjalan di atas kaca.

10.en: Outside, the spider still hadn't moved its body. Only its head followed the sound, the two great front eyes tilted up toward the roof.
10.id: Di luar, laba-laba itu masih belum menggerakkan tubuhnya. Hanya kepalanya yang mengikuti suara, kedua mata depannya yang besar mendongak ke arah atap.

11.en: Then, slowly, they tilted back down, and found Aiden.
11.id: Lalu, perlahan, kedua mata itu turun lagi, dan menemukan Aiden.

12.en: Sarah's voice came through his wrist, low and tight.
12.id: Suara Sarah terdengar dari pergelangan Jack, rendah dan tegang.

14.en: I know. Aiden, keep going. Same speed. Don't look at it.
14.id: Aku tahu. Aiden, jalan terus. Kecepatan sama. Jangan lihat dia.

15.en: How am I supposed to not look at it?
15.id: Gimana caranya aku tidak melihat dia?

17.en: Aiden looked at the tomatoes. He kept walking. It took him forever, and Jack didn't breathe for most of it.
17.id: Aiden melihat tomat-tomat itu. Ia terus berjalan. Rasanya makan waktu selamanya, dan sepanjang sebagian besar waktu itu Jack tidak bernapas.

18.en: When he reached the front door, he slid open a gray panel on the wall and pressed his palm flat against a switch. The vent motors changed pitch. All along the roof, the steel arms began to pull, and the glass panels began to lower.
18.id: Begitu sampai di pintu depan, ia menggeser terbuka sebuah panel abu-abu di dinding dan menekankan telapak tangannya rata ke sebuah sakelar. Nada motor-motor ventilasi berubah. Di sepanjang atap, lengan-lengan baja mulai menarik, dan panel-panel kaca mulai turun.

20.en: At the far north end, three vents stayed exactly where they were, wide open to the sky.
20.id: Di ujung paling utara, tiga ventilasi tetap persis di tempatnya, terbuka lebar ke langit.

21.en: Aiden pressed the switch again. Nothing.
21.id: Aiden menekan sakelar lagi. Tidak terjadi apa-apa.

23.en: Lena's voice came through Jack's wrist, quick and certain.
23.id: Suara Lena terdengar dari pergelangan Jack, cepat dan yakin.

24.en: They won't. Those three are on the west feeder. I isolated it last night. It was one of the three faults.
24.id: Memang tidak akan. Tiga itu ada di jalur pengumpan barat. Semalam aku mengisolasinya. Itu salah satu dari tiga gangguan tadi.

25.en: Can you turn it back on?

26.en: Not from here, and not without knowing why it faulted in the first place. If I push power into a damaged line, I could start a fire in a building full of dry seedling trays.
26.id: Tidak dari sini, dan tidak tanpa tahu kenapa jalurnya bermasalah sejak awal. Kalau aku memaksa listrik masuk ke jalur yang rusak, aku bisa memicu kebakaran di bangunan yang penuh baki bibit kering.

29.en: There's a crank on each vent. From the catwalk.
29.id: Ada engkol di setiap ventilasi. Dari titian.

30.en: Jack followed his finger. A narrow steel catwalk ran the length of the roof peak, reached by a ladder bolted to the north wall. Each vent had a small hand crank mounted beside its hinge.
30.id: Jack mengikuti arah jarinya. Sebuah titian baja yang sempit membentang sepanjang puncak atap, dicapai lewat tangga yang dibaut ke dinding utara. Setiap ventilasi punya engkol tangan kecil yang terpasang di samping engselnya.

31.en: The north wall was the one closest to the grass.
31.id: Dinding utara adalah dinding yang paling dekat dengan rumput.

36.en: Jack nodded toward a red fire extinguisher hanging beside the irrigation valves.
36.id: Jack mengangguk ke arah sebuah alat pemadam api merah yang tergantung di samping katup-katup irigasi.

37.en: You're the one who knows what to do down here if something comes through. That's carbon dioxide. Cold, loud, and it'll startle almost anything. If you have to use it, aim at the face, not the body.
37.id: Kamu yang tahu harus berbuat apa di bawah sini kalau ada yang menerobos masuk. Itu karbon dioksida. Dingin, berisik, dan bisa mengagetkan hampir apa saja. Kalau terpaksa memakainya, arahkan ke wajah, jangan ke badan.

38.en: Mark took the extinguisher off the wall and checked the pin.
38.id: Mark menurunkan alat pemadam itu dari dinding dan memeriksa pinnya.

41.en: That's longer than I usually get.
41.id: Itu lebih lama daripada yang biasanya kudapat.

42.en: Jack walked to the ladder. Slowly. Every step deliberate. He could feel the spider's attention follow him the way he would feel the sun on the side of his face.
42.id: Jack berjalan ke tangga. Pelan. Setiap langkah disengaja. Ia bisa merasakan perhatian laba-laba itu mengikutinya, seperti merasakan sinar matahari di sisi wajahnya.

43.en: Aiden whispered from the front door, just loud enough to carry.
43.id: Aiden berbisik dari pintu depan, cukup keras untuk terdengar.

44.en: Doctor Bennett. Slow is invisible. Fast is food.
44.id: Dokter Bennett. Pelan itu tak terlihat. Cepat itu makanan.

46.en: I'm serious. That's how they see. Anything that moves fast looks like something to eat.
46.id: Aku serius. Begitu cara mereka melihat. Apa pun yang bergerak cepat kelihatan seperti sesuatu untuk dimakan.

48.en: The ladder was cold under his hands. At the top, the catwalk swayed slightly under his weight. Through the open vents, the morning smelled green and enormous, like a forest after rain.
48.id: Tangga itu dingin di tangannya. Di atas, titian sedikit bergoyang di bawah bobotnya. Lewat ventilasi yang terbuka, pagi tercium hijau dan luar biasa luas, seperti hutan sehabis hujan.

49.en: He reached the first crank and began to turn it.
49.id: Ia meraih engkol pertama dan mulai memutarnya.

50.en: It was stiff. The panel lowered by a few centimeters with every turn, the hinge creaking. Jack kept his shoulders still and moved only his wrists, one slow rotation at a time, until the glass met the frame with a soft click.
50.id: Engkolnya keras. Panel itu turun beberapa sentimeter setiap putaran, engselnya berderit. Jack menjaga bahunya tetap diam dan hanya menggerakkan pergelangan tangan, satu putaran pelan demi satu putaran pelan, sampai kaca bertemu bingkainya dengan bunyi klik yang lembut.

51.en: From his wrist, Sarah counted quietly.

54.en: Below him, the moths had begun to stir. The sun had reached the western glass now, and the insects clinging there were warming, their wings opening and closing in slow, lazy beats. A fly crawled up the outside of the roof, right beside the third vent, and sat there in a patch of sunlight, cleaning its face with its front legs.
54.id: Di bawahnya, ngengat-ngengat mulai bergerak. Matahari sudah mencapai kaca sisi barat sekarang, dan serangga-serangga yang menempel di sana mulai hangat, sayap mereka membuka dan menutup dalam kepakan lambat dan malas. Seekor lalat merayap naik di sisi luar atap, tepat di samping ventilasi ketiga, lalu diam di sepetak sinar matahari, membersihkan wajahnya dengan kaki depan.

55.en: Halfway through the second crank, Sarah's voice changed.
55.id: Di tengah putaran engkol kedua, suara Sarah berubah.

57.en: He didn't look down. He kept turning.
57.id: Ia tidak menunduk. Ia terus memutar.

59.en: It's standing up. It's on the pavement now. It's… it's turning toward the roof.
59.id: Dia berdiri. Sekarang dia di jalan aspal. Dia… dia berbalik ke arah atap.

62.en: The second vent clicked shut. Jack slid one foot along the catwalk, then the other, until he was beside the third. The fly was less than an arm's length away on the far side of the open gap, glossy and enormous, its huge red eyes catching the light.
62.id: Ventilasi kedua menutup dengan bunyi klik. Jack menggeser satu kaki di sepanjang titian, lalu kaki yang lain, sampai ia berada di samping ventilasi ketiga. Lalat itu kurang dari sejangkauan lengan jauhnya di sisi lain celah yang terbuka, mengilap dan sangat besar, mata merahnya yang besar menangkap cahaya.

64.en: Sarah's voice dropped to almost nothing.
64.id: Suara Sarah turun hingga nyaris tak terdengar.

67.en: Below, Mark said something he didn't catch. Then the whole greenhouse boomed like a drum.
67.id: Di bawah, Mark mengatakan sesuatu yang tidak tertangkap olehnya. Lalu seluruh rumah kaca berdentum seperti genderang.

68.en: The roof shuddered. Dust and grit rained from the steel ribs. Directly above Jack's head, a pane of glass cracked into a white star with a sound like ice breaking on a lake.
68.id: Atap bergetar. Debu dan pasir berjatuhan dari rusuk-rusuk baja. Tepat di atas kepala Jack, sebuah panel kaca retak membentuk bintang putih, dengan bunyi seperti es yang pecah di danau.

69.en: And through that glass, a single meter away, was the spider.
69.id: Dan di balik kaca itu, hanya satu meter jauhnya, ada laba-laba itu.

70.en: It had landed on the roof as lightly and as heavily as a falling car. Its legs gripped the steel frame on either side. Its underside was pale and furred. And its face was right there, the two great eyes level with his own, dark and glossy and deep, and in each of them Jack could see a tiny curved reflection of a man standing perfectly still on a catwalk.
70.id: Ia mendarat di atap seringan sekaligus seberat mobil yang jatuh. Kaki-kakinya mencengkeram rangka baja di kedua sisi. Bagian bawah tubuhnya pucat dan berbulu. Dan wajahnya ada tepat di sana, kedua mata besarnya sejajar dengan mata Jack, gelap dan mengilap dan dalam, dan di masing-masing mata itu Jack bisa melihat pantulan kecil yang melengkung dari seorang laki-laki yang berdiri diam sempurna di atas titian.

72.en: Not the way a camera looked. The way a person looked when they were trying to decide what something was.
72.id: Bukan seperti kamera menatap. Seperti seseorang menatap ketika sedang berusaha memutuskan sesuatu itu apa.

74.en: Then the spider's front legs moved, faster than he could follow, and the fly was simply gone from the glass.
74.id: Lalu kaki-kaki depan laba-laba itu bergerak, lebih cepat daripada yang bisa diikuti matanya, dan lalat itu begitu saja lenyap dari kaca.

75.en: The spider held it for a moment, as though considering. Then it turned, stepped across the roof with a slow rolling grace that sent faint vibrations through the catwalk under Jack's feet, and dropped off the far side.
75.id: Laba-laba itu memegangnya sesaat, seolah sedang menimbang. Lalu ia berbalik, melangkah melintasi atap dengan keanggunan lambat yang bergulir, yang mengirim getaran samar ke titian di bawah kaki Jack, lalu turun dari sisi seberang.

76.en: When Jack finally looked down through the western glass, the grass was swaying where it had gone in. Then it was still.
76.id: Ketika Jack akhirnya melihat ke bawah lewat kaca sisi barat, rumput bergoyang di tempat makhluk itu masuk. Lalu diam.

77.en: Sarah's voice came through, not quite steady.
77.id: Suara Sarah terdengar, belum sepenuhnya mantap.

78.en: It's gone. Jack, it's gone. It went back into the grass.
78.id: Dia sudah pergi. Jack, dia sudah pergi. Dia kembali ke rumput.

79.en: Jack let out a breath he felt all the way to his knees. He reached up and cranked the third vent closed, one slow rotation at a time, because it felt wrong to hurry now, and only when the glass clicked into the frame did he notice the blood running across the back of his left hand.
79.id: Jack mengembuskan napas yang terasa sampai ke lututnya. Ia menjangkau ke atas dan memutar engkol ventilasi ketiga sampai tertutup, satu putaran pelan demi satu putaran pelan, karena rasanya salah untuk terburu-buru sekarang, dan baru ketika kaca berbunyi klik di bingkainya ia menyadari darah yang mengalir di punggung tangan kirinya.

80.en: A sliver from the cracked pane. He hadn't even felt it.
80.id: Serpihan dari panel yang retak. Ia bahkan tidak merasakannya.

84.en: Everything's small. That's the whole problem.

85.en: Jack climbed down. Aiden was sitting on the floor beside the front door with the fogger in his lap and his back against the wall. He looked up at Jack the way people looked at someone who had just walked out of a car accident.
85.id: Jack turun. Aiden duduk di lantai di samping pintu depan dengan alat pengasap di pangkuannya dan punggung bersandar ke dinding. Ia mendongak menatap Jack seperti orang menatap seseorang yang baru saja keluar dari kecelakaan mobil.

86.en: Aiden's voice was barely above a whisper.

89.en: They do that. When they're small. They look at you like they're thinking about it.
89.id: Mereka memang begitu. Waktu masih kecil. Mereka menatapmu seolah sedang memikirkannya.

91.en: That you weren't a fly, probably.

93.en: Sarah's voice came through his wrist again, steadier now, and quick, the way it got when an idea had already started.
93.id: Suara Sarah kembali terdengar dari pergelangannya, lebih mantap sekarang, dan cepat, seperti biasanya kalau sebuah gagasan sudah mulai bergulir.

94.en: Jack. It jumped. It didn't walk to the fly. It jumped onto the roof from the pavement.
94.id: Jack. Dia melompat. Dia tidak berjalan ke lalat itu. Dia melompat ke atap dari jalan aspal.

98.en: And no trail. Like the mark you found by the southern perimeter.
98.id: Dan tanpa jejak. Seperti bekas yang kamu temukan di dekat perimeter selatan.

101.en: Something hit the ground outside the settlement last night. Twice. It left a print and no tracks.
101.id: Ada sesuatu yang menghantam tanah di luar permukiman semalam. Dua kali. Meninggalkan cetakan, tanpa jejak kaki.

103.en: That wasn't this one. Or not because it was hunting. Jumpers don't hunt in the dark. They need light to see.
103.id: Itu bukan yang ini. Atau bukan karena dia sedang berburu. Pelompat tidak berburu dalam gelap. Mereka butuh cahaya untuk melihat.

104.en: For a moment, nobody said anything.
104.id: Sesaat, tak ada yang berkata apa-apa.

105.en: So something else out there jumps.
105.id: Jadi ada hal lain di luar sana yang melompat.

106.en: Or something else out there lands. We don't know yet. Write it down. Both.
106.id: Atau ada hal lain di luar sana yang mendarat. Kita belum tahu. Catat. Dua-duanya.

107.en: Jack wrapped his hand in a clean shop rag from Aiden's bench and looked at the cracked pane in the roof, the white star spreading across it like frost.
107.id: Jack membalut tangannya dengan lap bengkel bersih dari meja kerja Aiden dan memandang panel retak di atap, bintang putih yang menjalar di permukaannya seperti bunga es.

108.en: Sarah. What did we just learn?
108.id: Sarah. Apa yang barusan kita pelajari?

110.en: It's an animal. It came here for food, and it took food, and it left. It didn't break in because it didn't want to. It never cared about us. That's rule one. It's an animal. It does what animals do.
110.id: Itu hewan. Dia datang ke sini untuk makanan, dia mengambil makanan, lalu pergi. Dia tidak menerobos masuk karena dia tidak mau. Dia tidak pernah peduli pada kita. Itu aturan pertama. Itu hewan. Dia melakukan apa yang dilakukan hewan.

112.en: Nobody attacks anything. Aiden, that includes you.
112.id: Tidak ada yang menyerang apa pun. Aiden, itu termasuk kamu.

113.en: Aiden held up the fogger and set it carefully on the floor.
113.id: Aiden mengangkat alat pengasapnya dan meletakkannya hati-hati di lantai.

114.en: Three. No lights shining outward along the edge after dark. The lights brought the insects, and the insects brought the spider.
114.id: Ketiga. Tidak ada lampu yang menyorot keluar di sepanjang tepian setelah gelap. Lampu mengundang serangga, dan serangga mengundang laba-laba.

117.en: Then we put blackout blinds on the western glass at night. The plants get their light. The island doesn't see it.
117.id: Kalau begitu kita pasang tirai gelap di kaca sisi barat pada malam hari. Tanamannya tetap dapat cahaya. Pulau ini tidak melihatnya.

118.en: Four. Anything an insect can fit through gets closed. Vents, cracks, drains. Doors.
118.id: Keempat. Apa pun yang bisa dilewati serangga harus ditutup. Ventilasi, retakan, saluran pembuangan. Pintu.

119.id: Kelima. Bergerak pelan di dekat kaca.

120.en: Jack looked at Mark, then at Aiden.

121.id: Keenam. Tidak ada yang keluar sendirian.

122.en: There was a pause on the line.

124.en: I've been writing since rule one.
124.id: Aku sudah mencatat sejak aturan pertama.

125.en: Mark's radio crackled before Jack could answer. A voice he didn't recognize, young and tense.
125.id: Radio Mark berderak sebelum Jack sempat menjawab. Suara yang tidak ia kenali, muda dan tegang.

126.en: Jones, this is Unit Four. Are you near the west side?
126.id: Jones, ini Unit Empat. Kamu di dekat sisi barat?

129.en: Whatever that bang was, half the west side heard it. I've got people coming out of their houses. They're walking toward the community center. Forty, maybe fifty, and more behind them.
129.id: Apa pun dentuman tadi, separuh sisi barat mendengarnya. Orang-orang keluar dari rumah. Mereka berjalan ke balai warga. Empat puluh, mungkin lima puluh, dan masih ada lagi di belakang mereka.

130.en: Mark looked at Jack. Jack looked at the cracked glass, and the swaying grass beyond it, and the empty pavement where the spider had sat.
130.id: Mark memandang Jack. Jack memandang kaca yang retak, dan rumput yang bergoyang di baliknya, dan jalan aspal kosong tempat laba-laba itu tadi mendekam.

131.en: Unit Four, what are they saying?

132.en: A short pause on the channel.

133.en: They're asking for Doctor Bennett. By name.
133.id: Mereka mencari Dokter Bennett. Menyebut namanya.
